newsitem.title: USA: Angeion case yields another guilty plea.
newsitem.headline: Angeion case yields another guilty plea.

text.p: Robert Maietta pleaded guilty to two counts of securities fraud in connection with trading in shares of Angeion Corp, according to a statement issued Monday by the U.S Attorney's office in St. Paul.
Maietta, 48, a businessman, admitted in court that he had tried to keep the price of Angeion stock high by placing a false order with a brokerage firm, the statement said.
Angeion, a Plymouth, Minn.-based company, develops and makes devices for angioplasty and other cardiac procedures.
The price of Angeion's stock rose from March through July 1991 and then collapsed, with the company losing $58 million in market value in a little more than three months.
U.S. Attorney David Lillehaug, in a suit filed in June 1996, had originally charged seven people with securities and wire fraud. Six individuals have already pleaded guilty.
"These convictions send a strong message to Minnesota's securities community that honesty in the marketplace is paramount and that the cheaters will be prosecuted," Lillehaug said in a statement.
Maietta faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and/or a $250,000 fine, the U.S. Attorney's office said.
Shares of Angeion closed off 5/16 to 4-1/16.
